excerpt: D-ID makes AI avatar videos and interactive visual agents. Its Agentic Videos feature lets viewers ask a video questions and get spoken answers from an avatar. What it does, pricing notes and alternatives.
content:
D-ID is an AI video company that turns photos, text and audio into talking avatar videos and real-time, interactive avatars it calls visual agents. You can use it through its Creative Reality Studio, an API or integrations such as its PowerPoint plugin. D-ID says it was founded in 2017, that its studio and API have produced more than 200 million avatar videos, and that it acquired the explainer-video company simpleshow in 2025. Its legal entities are De-Identification Ltd. and De-Identification Inc., according to its privacy policy.

The feature launched on Product Hunt, Agentic Videos, makes an ordinary video interactive. You upload a video in the Studio, choose a video agent and set how the conversation starts. Viewers can then stop and ask questions by voice or chat, and the agent answers using the video's script and any extra knowledge you add, so a training clip, product demo or tutorial can take follow-up questions. D-ID says the agents run on its V4 architecture with sub-second latency, and that you can see which questions viewers ask. Agentic Videos launched on 18 June 2026, D-ID's seventh launch on Product Hunt, and finished #7 for the day with 180 points and 57 comments.

We have not tested D-ID ourselves. This page brings together D-ID's official site, its Product Hunt page and the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.starts_at: 14-day free trial; paid from $5.9/month ($4.7/month billed annually)
profile.summary_short: AI avatar videos and interactive video agents; Agentic Videos let viewers ask a video questions

gallery.alt: D-ID Creative Reality Studio video editor with an avatar presenter, a script panel and a row of presenters to choose from
D-ID graphic 'Build and deploy interactive AI Agents', showing a chat with an illustrated avatar agent in the Studio
D-ID Studio language menu for an avatar's script, captioned 'Choose between 120 languages for your avatar's script'

fit: make training, onboarding or product-demo videos and want viewers to be able to ask follow-up questions inside the video
need avatar videos or agents in many languages (D-ID says 120+)
want to embed a talking agent on your own site or build one into an app through an API
not_fit: need watermark-free output on a free or entry plan: D-ID's FAQ says Trial and Lite videos carry a watermark, full-screen for trial users
want unused minutes to roll over: they reset each month
want a public agent without usage costs: conversations other people have with your shared agent are charged to your account

pricing.intro: D-ID's Studio pricing page lists a free trial, three paid plans and Enterprise, in US dollars. Each paid plan is cheaper per month when billed annually. Prices below are the page's default (smallest) credit option; the cards also offer larger credit amounts.

plans.name: Trial
plans.detail: 14-day trial. 3 minutes for videos, agents, Video Translate and API; full-screen watermark; personal-use licence

plans.name: Lite
plans.detail: Or $4.7/month billed annually ($56 a year). 10 minutes a month; D-ID watermark

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: Or $16/month billed annually ($191 a year). 15 minutes a month, premium voices, 1 voice clone, commercial-use licence

plans.name: Advanced
plans.detail: Or $108/month billed annually ($1,293 a year). 100 minutes a month, 3 voice clones, custom logo

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Unlimited video minutes, custom minutes for agents and API, professional voice cloning, customer success manager

notes: When we checked, the Lite, Pro and Advanced cards also offered unlimited videos for the first month, subject to D-ID's fair-use policy; this is a promotion, not a permanent feature.
Plans are measured in video minutes. Each video is rounded up to the nearest 15 seconds, and unused minutes do not carry over.
Trial and Lite videos carry a D-ID watermark; trial users get a full-screen watermark.
API usage draws from the same minute balance as the Studio.
When you share an agent, other people's conversations with it are charged to your account.

alternatives.intro: These are products Product Hunt lists as alternatives to D-ID. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: HeyGen
items.starts_at: Free to start; see its pricing page
items.difference: Centred on lifelike personal avatars for recorded videos. D-ID's launch adds Q&A inside an existing video.

items.name: DeepBrain AI
items.what: AI Studios: avatars, dubbing, video generation and interactive avatars
items.difference: Also offers interactive, LLM-compatible avatars, alongside a large avatar library and dubbing in 150+ languages.

items.name: VEED
items.what: Online video editor with AI video, avatars and voice tools
items.difference: A general video editor with avatar features, not a platform for conversational agents.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Synthesia and Spiritme. D-ID's own benchmark page compares its real-time lip-sync with HeyGen, Anam and Tavus; that is D-ID's own test.

x.none: We did not check X for this profile.

faq.a: Videos that viewers can talk to. You upload a video in D-ID's Studio and attach a video agent; viewers ask questions by voice or chat and the agent answers from the script and any knowledge you add. The feature launched on Product Hunt on 18 June 2026.
Upload any video in D-ID's Creative Reality Studio, choose a video agent and define how the interaction should begin, according to D-ID.
Yes. D-ID says agents reply in the language you speak if a multilingual voice is enabled, and the Studio supports more than 120 languages.

faq.q: Can I put an agent on my website?
faq.a: Yes. You can share a D-ID-hosted link or embed the agent on your own site. Conversations others have with it are charged to your account.

faq.q: Do D-ID videos have a watermark?
faq.a: On the Trial and Lite plans, yes. D-ID says this is to be open about the synthetic nature of the videos.
An AI video company founded in 2017, which says its studio and API have produced more than 200 million avatar videos. It acquired simpleshow in 2025.
